title: Eyelash enhancement (bimatoprost)
summary: Counselling on bimatoprost (a prostamide) for longer, darker lashes: how it works, permanent iris darkening, reversible eyelid pigmentation and when to exclude a disease cause of lash loss.

what: **Eyelash enhancement** options include cosmetics, lifts and **bimatoprost** (a prostamide also used in glaucoma drops) applied to the upper lid margin to lengthen lashes.
cause: Bimatoprost increases eyelash length, thickness and darkness by **extending anagen** and stimulating follicle melanogenesis; periocular skin and iris melanocytes can also respond.

list: Longer, darker lashes over weeks to months.
Side effects: periocular hyperpigmentation, **iris colour change** (especially hazel/green eyes), itch, redness; periorbital fat atrophy (glaucoma-dose context).

diagnosis: Before use: exclude a disease cause of sparse lashes (**madarosis**): alopecia areata, thyroid disease, blepharitis, trichotillomania, chemotherapy.

head: Cause of sparse lashes
Clue
rows: Loss of the outer brows; systemic symptoms

list: Explain cosmetic versus glaucoma origins; apply only as directed to the upper lid margin, not into the eye for cosmetic use.
Warn about **permanent iris darkening**, reversible periocular skin darkening, possible hair growth on unintended skin if the product migrates, and ocular irritation.
Avoid with active ocular inflammation unless an ophthalmologist agrees; remove contact lenses as per product advice.
Effects reverse over weeks to months if stopped.
Check the current SmPC/BNF; this page does not cover off-label periocular protocols.

red_flags: Eye pain, redness or visual change: stop and seek ophthalmology review.
Patients on glaucoma drops: discuss with their ophthalmologist (additive effect on intraocular pressure).
pearls: Eyelash serums sold cosmetically vary widely; prescription bimatoprost needs proper counselling on iris pigment.
